political_axes.name: Left-Right
political_axes.scoring_rule: Not scored separately. Aggregated from each bill's per-category partisan_score. A YES vote on a bill with partisan_score s and impact i contributes s * i.

political_axes.name: Economic System

negative_pole.label: Collective / Public
negative_pole.description: Public provision, regulation of markets, and redistribution.

positive_pole.label: Market / Private
positive_pole.description: Private provision, deregulation, and market-set outcomes.

political_axes.scoring_rule: Score the mechanism a YES vote uses to achieve its goal: public vs. private provision, degree of market regulation, redistribution. Do not score the size of spending here.
boundary_rules: economic is the mechanism (public vs. private provision, regulation, redistribution); fiscal is the net size of spending or deficit. A deficit-financed tax cut is market (+) on economic and expansion (-) on fiscal. A defense spending increase is neutral on economic.
Tariffs, trade deals, and domestic-content rules are scored on trade only, not on economic.

anchor_examples.description: A bill creating a public health insurance option
A bill deregulating banks or privatizing a public service

political_axes.name: Fiscal

negative_pole.label: Spending Expansion
negative_pole.description: Increases net federal spending or deficits.

positive_pole.label: Fiscal Restraint
positive_pole.description: Cuts net federal spending or reduces deficits.

political_axes.scoring_rule: Score the net effect of a YES vote on federal spending and deficits, regardless of what the money is spent on or how it is delivered.
boundary_rules: fiscal is the net size of spending or deficit; economic is the mechanism. A deficit-financed tax cut is expansion (-) on fiscal and market (+) on economic.

anchor_examples.description: An omnibus package with large unpaid-for spending increases
A rescissions package or balanced-budget measure

political_axes.name: State Power

negative_pole.label: Libertarian
negative_pole.description: Limits coercion, surveillance, and punishment by the state.

positive_pole.label: Authoritarian
positive_pole.description: Expands coercion, surveillance, or punishment by the state.

political_axes.scoring_rule: Score how much coercive, surveillance, or punitive power a YES vote gives the state over people under U.S. jurisdiction.
boundary_rules: state_power is power over people under U.S. jurisdiction; security is posture toward foreign states and actors. FISA 702 can load on both.
state_power is how much coercion the state uses; social is which norms are promoted. A federal mandate for diversity training is progressive (-) on social and authoritarian (+) on state_power.

anchor_examples.description: A bill requiring warrants for government access to Americans' data
A bill expanding warrantless surveillance or mandatory minimum sentences

political_axes.name: Social

negative_pole.label: Progressive
negative_pole.description: Promotes newer or more inclusive social norms.

positive_pole.label: Traditional
positive_pole.description: Promotes established or traditional social norms.

political_axes.scoring_rule: Score which social norms a YES vote promotes, independent of how forcefully the state enforces them.
boundary_rules: social is which norms are promoted; state_power is how much coercion the state uses. They can disagree.

anchor_examples.description: A bill protecting same-sex marriage or expanding anti-discrimination coverage
A bill restricting abortion or protecting religious exemptions

political_axes.name: Security Posture

negative_pole.label: Restraint / Dovish
negative_pole.description: Reduces force, defense spending, or confrontation with foreign rivals.

positive_pole.label: Hawkish
positive_pole.description: Increases force, defense spending, or confrontation with foreign rivals.

political_axes.scoring_rule: Score posture toward foreign states and actors: use of force, defense spending, and confrontational measures such as sanctions, export controls, foreign-ownership bans, and app bans.
boundary_rules: security is force and confrontation; global is participation in institutions, treaties, and cooperation. NATO funding is hawkish (+) and multilateral (-).
security is posture toward foreign states and actors; state_power is power over people under U.S. jurisdiction.

anchor_examples.description: A war powers resolution ending U.S. involvement in a conflict
A bill banning a foreign-owned app or sanctioning a rival state

political_axes.name: Trade

negative_pole.label: Free Trade
negative_pole.description: Lowers tariffs and barriers to trade.

positive_pole.label: Protectionist
positive_pole.description: Raises tariffs or barriers to protect domestic industry.

political_axes.scoring_rule: Score the effect of a YES vote on barriers to cross-border trade: tariffs, quotas, trade agreements, and domestic-content rules.
boundary_rules: Tariffs, trade deals, and domestic-content rules are scored on trade only. Do not also score them on economic.

anchor_examples.description: A bill approving a free trade agreement or disapproving new tariffs
A bill imposing broad tariffs or buy-American requirements

political_axes.name: Global Engagement

negative_pole.label: Multilateral
negative_pole.description: Deeper participation in international institutions, treaties, and cooperation.

positive_pole.label: Sovereigntist
positive_pole.description: Preserves national autonomy and limits international commitments.

political_axes.scoring_rule: Score participation in international institutions, treaties, and cooperative arrangements, not the use of force.
boundary_rules: global is participation in institutions and cooperation; security is force and confrontation. NATO funding is hawkish (+) and multilateral (-).

anchor_examples.description: A bill rejoining an international climate or health agreement
A bill withdrawing from an international organization

political_axes.name: Institutional
political_axes.scoring_rule: Computed from roll call votes, never scored by an LLM. Weighted rate at which a member votes against their party's leadership position, mapped to -1..1.
boundary_rules: institutional is whether the member voted with party leadership; executive_power is what a bill does to branch powers. They are unrelated mechanisms.

political_axes.name: Branch Power

negative_pole.label: Legislative Checks
negative_pole.description: Strengthens Congress's checks on the executive branch.

positive_pole.label: Executive Deference
positive_pole.description: Expands or defers to executive authority.

political_axes.scoring_rule: Score what a YES vote does to the balance of power between Congress and the executive branch: war, tariff, and spending authority, agency discretion, executive orders.
boundary_rules: executive_power is what the bill does to branch powers; institutional is whether the member voted with party leadership. Unrelated mechanisms.

anchor_examples.description: A bill requiring congressional approval for emergency tariffs
A bill delegating broad discretionary authority to an agency or the President

political_axes.name: Federalism

negative_pole.label: Centralized
negative_pole.description: Shifts authority to the federal government.

positive_pole.label: Decentralized
positive_pole.description: Shifts authority to states and localities.

political_axes.scoring_rule: Score where a YES vote places decision-making authority between the federal government and the states and localities.

anchor_examples.description: A bill setting national standards that preempt state law
A bill block-granting a federal program to the states
